title: GNG Electronics Ltd - 544455 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GNG Electronics Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to INR651.7 crore, with PAT nearly tripling to INR42.1 crore and PAT margin at 6.5%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter on record, with consolidated revenue up 43% YoY to INR651.7 crore, EBITDA margin at 9.8% (up about 307 bps) and PAT of INR42.1 crore (PAT margin 6.5%, up about 323 bps). For FY26, revenue grew 34% to INR1,891 crore, PAT rose 91% to INR132 crore and PAT margin reached 7%. Management attributed gains to better procurement, inventory positioning and realisations, and framed rising global PC component prices and an expected 2026 PC shipment decline as a structural tailwind for refurbished laptops. Net debt fell to about INR300 crore at March-end from INR466 crore in December, while inventory rose to about INR743 crore and debtor days moved up to about 40. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of around 25% and PAT margin expansion of at least 50 bps.

segments.name: Laptops (volume and ASP)
segments.commentary: FY26 laptop ASP about INR28,800 and Q4 laptop ASP about INR30,000 (vs about INR29,000 in Q3); laptops are about 81% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Other products (non-laptop)
segments.commentary: FY26 ASP about INR18,300; Q4 ASP about INR19,000; about 19% of FY26 revenue. Q4 volume was about 65,000 units.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: About 33% of FY26 revenue. Consumption revenue rose to INR622 crore from INR345 crore, up 80%.

segments.name: US, Europe, UAE, rest of world
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue split: US about 21%, Europe about 20% (together about 41%), UAE about 12%, rest of world about 14%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: revenue growth of around 25%, with management calling it conservative.
FY27 guidance: PAT margin expansion of at least 50 bps from the FY26 level of 7%.
EBITDA margin implied at about 11.5% (from 10.6%) to deliver the 50 bps PAT expansion, per CFO.
Management expects a sequential margin improvement quarter-on-quarter from Q1 FY27, with Q4 seasonally subdued due to volume push.
Net debt trajectory expected at around INR300 crore; management sees no need for equity capital through FY28-FY29.
Component prices expected to keep rising through end-2027 and not fall before January 2028 per management view.
capex_capacity: Refurbishment capacity about 150,000 units per month, vs FY26 run-rate of about 60,000-61,000 units per month (727,000 units in FY26).
Mumbai: one facility expanded to two. UAE: facilities increased from three to eight.
Employee count about 2,148 at March 2026 (about 1,800 production technicians), up from about 1,200 a year earlier; significant additions in the last three to four months.
No additional manufacturing facility planned in FY27; space already secured. Marketing headcount being expanded, with marketing a higher priority.
Shipments inward and outward are by air; management says the UAE operations and shipping have been unaffected by regional conflict.
demand_pricing: FY26 volume about 727,000 units vs about 590,000 in FY25; Q4 volume about 241,000 (about 176,000 laptops and 65,000 others).
Component price increases cited: 8GB DDR5 module from USD23.35 (Oct 1, 2025) to about USD120 (Apr 1, 2026); 1TB SSD from about USD70 to about USD249; high-end processor about 45% higher.
Entry-level new laptop channel price in India rose from about INR25,500 (Dec 2025) to about INR40,000 currently, about 57% higher.
IDC forecasts 2026 global PC shipments to fall about 11% (about 32 million units); management cites a 55-60 million unit gap versus expected growth.
Management expects the price of new laptops to keep rising; realisations expected to improve, though volume was prioritised over margin in Q4.
New distributors (Ingram, Supertron) added in February 2026; management said their contribution is a very small percentage so far. Distributors hold 30-45 days of inventory of new products.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin not follow the ASP increase versus Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 always carries a volume push over margin and cited people and process investments; ASP rose from about INR29,000 to INR30,000 for laptops and blended from INR26,200 to INR27,000 QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high (about INR700 crore+) and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose to about INR743 crore (from INR490 crore a year earlier) as a strategic buy-ahead of component price increases; management expects elevated inventory to persist near term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debtor days rise to about 40, and will they stay there?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit is needed to attract distributors used to new-PC OEM credit terms of 30-45 days; management intends to hold debtor days at current levels and not increase them further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance and EBITDA implication?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is about 25% revenue growth and at least 50 bps PAT margin expansion; CFO said EBITDA margin would be a shade higher, around 11.5% from 10.6%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of West Asia conflict on Sharjah operations and shipments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said facilities operated daily, shipments are by air with only minor delays, and there has been no operational impact on sourcing or production.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost run-rate and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly finance cost of about INR14-15 crore is likely to sustain, with net debt trending toward about INR300 crore after falling from INR466 crore in December.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: inventory about INR743 crore and debtors about INR206 crore; a sharp fall in component prices could hit the value of inventory, though management says input costs were held down.
Rising finance cost (about INR14-15 crore per quarter, up from about INR9 crore) as borrowings are used to fund inventory.
Regional geopolitical risk in the UAE (Sharjah facility, about 12% of revenue) despite management saying operations are normal.
Other expenses up about 37% (freight, marketing, insurance), with Q4 freight elevated; watch whether this moderates.
Q4 margin seasonality: management says Q1 FY27 margin should be slightly above Q4 FY26, but this depends on volume push and pricing.
Limited visibility on new distributor contribution (Ingram, Supertron, and pending European and US partnerships).
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on demand and structural tailwinds, with management repeatedly calling guidance conservative. Less specific when asked about distributor revenue, the margin trajectory and the Middle East situation, where answers were brief or qualitative.
key_quotes: Demand isn't the bottleneck, trust is, and we are solving for trust.
Trust premium is the high margin lever.
we have to buy ahead of the price increase curve and the need of the hour is to keep high levels of inventory.
we say that yes, this number is almost 3-4 months of quantum, but we see this as the real opportunity and enhance our profitability going forward.
